title: Bug: LRH upstream neighbors route-churn when using existing t2 j2 templates
author: Javier-Tan
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

While using the existing j2 templates for lrh (lrh-core.j2 -> t2-leaf.j2, lrh-leaf.j2 -> t2-core.j2), we are experiencing route churcning on upstream neighbors (FRH and URH)

### Steps to Reproduce

Perform `redeploy-topo` + `deploy-mg` for LRH device, wait a while for route churn to happen (may be more common after link flap)

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Route churn shouldn't happen

```shell

```

comments.author: yxieca
comments.body:
**AI review — Changes requested**

### Blocking

- Symlink-to-file fork with no divergence rationale (ansible/roles/eos/templates/lrh-core.j2, mode change 120000 → 100644, +159 lines): the whole point of the prior symlink was that LRH stayed in lockstep with t2-leaf.j2. The head file has only a top comment about multi-VRF routing to ceos_converged.j2 (lines 1–2) and no comment at all justifying why the non-converged body must diverge from t2-leaf.j2. Either (a) drop allowas-in in t2-leaf.j2 and keep the symlink, (b) render lrh from t2-leaf.j2 via include/macro and override just the neighbor stanza, or (c) add an explicit header comment (referencing #25727) stating LRH must not carry allowas-in and this file is intentionally forked.
- Fix vs. PR description is not verifiable from this diff (ansible/roles/eos/templates/lrh-core.j2, neighbor block at head lines ~117–130): the PR says "Remove allowas-in from the EOS neighbor configurations," but because the previous content lived behind a symlink, the diff shows only the new file, not a removal. The neighbor stanza at head lines 117–130 contains no allowas-in, which is consistent with the intent, but the reviewer cannot see it being removed. Please either (i) point to the t2-leaf.j2 line that carried allowas-in, or (ii) include the explicit before/after in the PR description so the fix is auditable.

### Grounded nits

- Unconditional include of ceos_converged.j2 (lines 3–5): {% if topo_is_multi_vrf ... %}{% include 'ceos_converged.j2' %} runs regardless of vm_type, while the rest of the file branches on vm_type == "ceos" (lines 8, 15, 60). If multi-VRF on LRH is ceos-only, either add the vm_type == "ceos" guard or add a comment stating multi-VRF LRH is ceos-only by construction.
- Unguarded host['bp_interface'] deref (lines 92–101): host['bp_interface']['ipv4'] is defined / host['bp_interface']['ipv6'] is defined dereference bp_interface before checking its existence; if bp_interface is ever absent on an LRH host this raises UndefinedError. If it is always populated for LRH, a one-line comment saying so is enough; otherwise gate with host['bp_interface'] is defined and host['bp_interface']['ipv4'] is defined.
- Stray leading space on the confederation {% endif %} (line 116 " {% endif %}"): produces an extra whitespace line in rendered output. Left-align and/or use whitespace-trim markers.
- Empty branch + missing space in disable_ceos_mgmt_gateway test (line 50): {% if disable_ceos_mgmt_gateway is defined and disable_ceos_mgmt_gateway == 'yes'%} has no body and a missing space before %}. Collapse to a clearer if/elif or invert the condition.
- Port-Channel min-links computed from all Ethernet* (lines 68–72, 79–82): ns.po_mbr_cnt counts every Ethernet* on the host and applies 75% as min-links to every Port-Channel. On a host with multiple Port-Channels or with non-member Ethernet interfaces this overcounts; consider computing per-PC from members, or documenting the assumption of a single PC.
- IPv6 AF activates only IPv6 peers with no explicit IPv4 AF block (lines 124–128, 131–137): parity with the previous t2-leaf.j2 rendering is worth a quick eyeball to confirm the IPv4 default AF is still what LRH wants.

---
Reviewed by AI agent on behalf of Ying.
